input.quote: This Agreement will be governed by the substantive laws of the State of New York, without regard for its conflict of laws provisions.
input.rationale: § 14.3 selects New York substantive law, which satisfies our preferred governing law. However, the Agreement nominates no dispute forum anywhere: searches for jurisdiction, venue, courts and arbitration return only a court-of-competent-jurisdiction reference in the Customer indemnity (§ 8.2) and the severability clause (§ 14.5); § 14.4 (jury waiver) and § 14.14 (two-year actions period) are procedural only and are not double-flagged. Both the preferred and fallback positions require a specified forum, so the silence on venue is a material shortfall rather than a minor sub-element (it is not walk-away territory, since there is no foreign venue or foreign-seated arbitration). We therefore add a single sentence fixing exclusive jurisdiction in the state and federal courts in New York County, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere, and leave the existing choice-of-law sentence verbatim.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement picks New York law but names no dispute forum, so we add exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, with the customary carve-out for temporary injunctive relief. This matches our preferred governing-law and venue position and leaves the existing choice-of-law sentence untouched.

ops.text: The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York will have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits of any dispute arising out of or related to this Agreement, provided that either party may seek temporary injunctive relief in any other court of competent jurisdiction.
